1570.task: Construct sparse-vector objects and implement dotProduct(other). Return the sum of coordinatewise products over equal-length vectors, exploiting sparsity where useful. Missing sparse entries represent zero.

1580.task: Boxes may be reordered and inserted into a warehouse from either end. A box must fit under every room ceiling traversed from its chosen entrance, and each room holds at most one box. Return the maximum number that can be stored. This differs from the left-entry-only variant.

1586.task: Implement a BST iterator supporting hasNext/next and hasPrev/prev in inorder order. The initial cursor is before the first element; next advances and returns, while prev moves back and returns. hasPrev is false before a previous returned position exists. Verify valid-call guarantees rather than inventing wraparound behavior.

1597.task: Build a binary expression tree from an infix arithmetic string with digits, parentheses and +,-,*,/. Leaves are operands; internal nodes are operators with left/right operands. Respect standard precedence and left associativity among operators of equal precedence. Verify unary operators and operand-width grammar before certification.

1602.task: Given a binary tree and a node u in it, return the next node immediately to u's right on the same level, or null if u is the level's rightmost node. Return the node reference.

1612.task: Given two expression trees whose internal nodes are addition and whose leaves are variables, determine whether they produce the same result for every assignment of variable values. Reordering and regrouping additions is allowed; repeated variable occurrences contribute multiplicity.

1618.task: Given text, available font sizes and a screen width/height, use FontInfo.getWidth(fontSize,char) and getHeight(fontSize) to find the largest available size fitting the complete text on one line. Return -1 if none fits. Character widths add; do not wrap text. Verify the font-metric monotonicity guarantee.

1628.task: Given a valid postfix arithmetic expression, build an expression tree whose evaluate method computes its integer result. Support +,-,*,/ with division truncated toward zero. Operand order matters for subtraction and division. The design should allow operators to be encapsulated by nodes rather than changing evaluation callers.

1634.task: Each polynomial is a linked list of nonzero coefficient/power terms in descending power order. Return a linked list for their sum in the same order, merging equal powers and omitting terms whose summed coefficient is zero.

1644.task: Given a binary tree and node references p and q that may not belong to it, return their lowest common ancestor only if both nodes are present. Otherwise return null. Compare node identity, not merely equal values.

1650.task: Given two nodes in the same binary tree with parent pointers, return their lowest common ancestor using those pointers. No root is supplied; a node is an ancestor of itself.

1660.task: One binary-tree node has an invalid right pointer referencing another node to its right at the same depth. Remove the defective node and its genuine subtree from its parent while preserving the separately referenced valid target subtree. Return the corrected root. Do not follow the corrupt pointer as though it were an actual child.

1676.task: Given a binary tree and a list of distinct node references known to occur in it, return the lowest common ancestor of every supplied node. A node is an ancestor of itself.

1682.task: Find the maximum length of a palindromic subsequence of a string that has even length and no equal adjacent characters except the central pair. Return zero if no nonempty valid subsequence exists.

1692.task: Distribute n distinct candies among k nonempty unlabeled bags. Count partitions of the candies into exactly k nonempty groups, modulo 1000000007. Swapping whole bags does not create a new distribution.

1698.task: Given a string, count its distinct nonempty contiguous substrings. Equal text at different positions counts only once.

1708.task: Given an integer array and k, return its lexicographically largest contiguous subarray of length k. The remembered domain has distinct values; verify that before relying only on first-element comparisons.

1724.task: Build a query structure over a weighted undirected graph. Each query(p,q,limit) asks whether some path connects p and q using only edges with weight strictly less than limit. Queries may arrive in any order; equal-to-limit edges are forbidden.

1730.task: In a grid, '*' is the starting position, '#' is food, 'O' is walkable and 'X' is blocked. Return the fewest four-direction steps to any food, or -1 if none is reachable. Verify uniqueness of the starting cell and the exact character contract.

1740.task: Given a binary tree with unique node values and two values known to be present, return the number of edges in the path between their nodes.

1746.task: Given an integer array, replace exactly one selected element by its square and then choose a nonempty contiguous subarray. Return the greatest achievable subarray sum. The squared element may be chosen as part of the maximizing segment; handle negative values without treating an empty segment as a valid answer.

1756.task: Implement MRUQueue initialized with values 1 through n. fetch(k) removes the kth current element using one-based indexing, appends it at the end, and returns its value. Every call uses the queue order resulting from previous calls.

1762.task: Buildings lie in a row with the ocean to their right. Return indices in ascending order of buildings taller than every building to their right. Equal-height buildings block the view; the rightmost building always qualifies.

1772.task: Given feature names and user-response strings, rank features by the number of distinct responses mentioning that feature as a word. Multiple mentions within one response count once. Preserve original feature order for equal popularity. Verify case and tokenization assumptions.

1778.task: Explore an unknown grid through GridMaster.canMove, move and isTarget. Return the minimum number of steps from the original position to the target, or -1 if unreachable. You cannot inspect a map directly. Exploration must track relative coordinates and physically backtrack so the discovered map is accurate.

1788.task: Given flower beauty values, choose a subsequence of at least two flowers whose first and last values are equal. Maximize the sum of selected values and return it. Intermediate flowers may be omitted but their order cannot change. Verify the guarantee that some matching endpoint pair exists.

1794.task: Given two strings, choose equal nonempty substrings, one from each, minimizing the absolute difference between their starting indices. Return the number of starting-index pairs that achieve this smallest difference and admit such a match. A length-one match is sufficient to witness a pair; do not count multiple lengths for one pair. Verify this remembered pair-count interpretation against the source.

1804.task: Implement a trie with insert(word), countWordsEqualTo(word), countWordsStartingWith(prefix) and erase(word). Store duplicate insertions with multiplicity. erase removes one occurrence, and calls are assumed to erase an existing occurrence. Prefix counts include every stored occurrence.

1810.task: Explore an unknown grid using a GridMaster interface with movement feasibility, target detection and movement costs. Find the minimum total cost from the original position to the target, or -1 if unreachable. Movement costs depend on the entered cell in the remembered contract; verify that interface detail before recording directed edges.

1820.task: Given a binary compatibility matrix between two groups, select the largest set of compatible pairs so no person belongs to more than one pair. Return the maximum matching size, not a greedy pairing count.

1826.task: Two sensors should record the same sequence, but one dropped a value and shifted subsequent observations left, ending with an arbitrary replacement value. Given both equal-length readings, identify which sensor is faulty, returning 1 or 2, or -1 if the available readings do not determine the faulty sensor uniquely. Verify the exact replacement-value guarantees and ambiguity rules.

1836.task: Given an unsorted linked list, remove every node whose value occurs more than once anywhere in the original list. Retain only globally unique values in original order; do not keep one representative of duplicates.

1842.task: Given a numeric string that is already a palindrome, return the smallest larger palindrome obtainable by rearranging exactly its digits. Return an empty string if no larger palindrome is possible. Preserve digit multiplicities and length.

1852.task: For each contiguous window of length k in an integer array, return its number of distinct values. Preserve window order.

1858.task: Given a list of words, return the longest word for which every nonempty prefix is also in the list. Break equal-length ties lexicographically; return an empty string if none qualifies.

1868.task: Two run-length-encoded arrays represent equal-length integer sequences using [value,frequency] pairs. Multiply the expanded sequences coordinatewise and return a run-length encoding of the products. Merge adjacent equal products and avoid expanding the inputs.

1874.task: Given two equal-length integer arrays, reorder their elements to minimize the sum of pairwise products at matching positions. Return that minimum product sum; preserve all occurrences.

1885.task: Given equal-length arrays nums1 and nums2, count index pairs i<j for which nums1[i]+nums1[j] is strictly greater than nums2[i]+nums2[j]. Equal sums do not qualify.

1891.task: Given ribbon lengths and positive k, cut ribbons into integer-length pieces, discarding leftovers, to obtain at least k equal-length pieces. Return the greatest positive piece length possible, or zero if no positive length yields k pieces.

1902.task: Insert distinct values into an initially empty BST in the supplied order. Return the depth of the final tree, measured in nodes from the root to the deepest leaf. Verify the source's value/permutation guarantees before choosing an indexed predecessor structure.

1908.task: Several heaps contain stones. Players alternate removing any positive number from a single heap, and a player with no move loses. Given initial heap sizes and optimal play, return whether the first player wins.

1918.task: Given a positive integer array and k, consider the sums of all nonempty contiguous subarrays, retaining duplicates from different positions. Return the kth smallest sum in that multiset.

1933.task: Given a digit string, decide whether it can be partitioned into same-digit blocks such that exactly one block has length two and every other block has length three. Blocks must be contiguous and consume the whole string.

1940.task: Given multiple sorted arrays of distinct integers, return their longest common subsequence. Because each is increasing, this is the sorted list of values present in every array. Verify the distinctness guarantee before treating the inputs as sets.

1950.task: For each window size k from 1 through n, find the minimum in every length-k contiguous subarray, then take the maximum of those minima. Return these n maxima in increasing window-size order.

1966.task: Count elements in an unsorted array that can always be found by a standard binary-search procedure regardless of pivot choices. Such an element must exceed every value to its left and be smaller than every value to its right. Verify the source's distinct-value guarantee before applying strict comparisons.

1973.task: Count binary-tree nodes whose value equals the sum of values of all their proper descendants. A leaf's descendant sum is zero, so a zero-valued leaf qualifies.

1983.task: Given two equal-length binary arrays, find the greatest length of an index interval whose element sum in the first array equals the sum over the same interval in the second. Return zero if there is no qualifying nonempty interval.

1989.task: A binary team array marks players as catchers or runners. Each catcher can catch at most one runner within absolute index distance dist, and each runner can be caught at most once. Return the greatest number of caught runners. Verify which bit denotes each team in the source before wiring the adapter.

1999.task: Given positive k and two allowed decimal digits, return the smallest integer strictly greater than k that is divisible by k and uses only those digits. Return -1 if no representable answer exists within the specified bound. Verify the exact integer cap and whether the two digits may coincide.

2015.task: Given buildings as [start,end,height] intervals, return maximal consecutive street segments on which the integer average height of covering buildings is constant. Omit uncovered segments and merge adjacent equal-average segments. Use half-open intervals and floor division for the average; verify the remembered rounding convention against the source.

2021.task: Each street light at position p with range r illuminates the inclusive integer interval [p-r,p+r]. Return the smallest integer position covered by the maximum number of lights.

2031.task: Given a binary array, count nonempty contiguous subarrays containing strictly more ones than zeros. Return the count modulo 1000000007.

2036.task: For a contiguous nonempty subarray, define its alternating sum by adding its first element, subtracting its second, adding its third, and so on. Return the largest such sum over all contiguous subarrays. Signs restart positive at each chosen start.

2046.task: A linked list is sorted by absolute node value. Rearrange it into ascending actual-value order, retaining every node. Return the new head; negative values must be placed before nonnegative ones in numeric order.

2052.task: Given a sentence with single spaces and a line width k, break it into lines without splitting words or reordering them. A non-final line costs the square of its unused character positions; the final line costs zero. Return the minimum total cost. Verify the guarantee that each word fits on a line.

2061.task: A robot starts at the top-left of a grid facing right. At each step it cleans its current open cell, moves forward if the next cell is open and in bounds, otherwise turns right by 90 degrees. Return the number of distinct cells cleaned before its position-and-direction state repeats. Verify starting-cell guarantees.

2067.task: Given a lowercase string and count, count nonempty contiguous substrings in which every character present occurs exactly count times. Characters absent from the substring impose no condition. Count positional occurrences, not just distinct substring texts.

2077.task: Given an undirected graph, count distinct three-room cycles. Each triangle counts once regardless of starting vertex or traversal direction. Verify that edges are simple and undirected before using degree intersections.

2083.task: Given a string, count nonempty contiguous substrings whose first and last characters are equal. Single-character substrings qualify; count occurrences by endpoints.

2093.task: Given a weighted undirected road graph, travel from city 0 to city n-1 with at most discounts coupons. A coupon halves one traversed road's toll using integer division, with at most one coupon per traversal. Return the minimum total toll, or -1 if unreachable.

2098.task: Choose a subsequence of exactly k elements from an integer array with an even total sum, maximizing that sum. Return the maximum sum, or -1 if no such subsequence exists. Verify the nonnegative domain before treating -1 as an unambiguous failure marker.

2107.task: Given a sequence of candy flavors, give away exactly k consecutive candies. Return the largest number of distinct flavors among the remaining candies. The removed block is contiguous; the retained candies may lie on both sides.

2123.task: Given a binary grid, remove the minimum number of 1 cells so that no two remaining 1s share a horizontal or vertical edge. Return that minimum removal count. Diagonal neighbors do not conflict.

2128.task: Given a binary matrix, decide whether it can become all zeros by any sequence of whole-row flips and whole-column flips. A flip replaces every bit on the chosen row or column by its complement.

2137.task: Buckets contain given nonnegative water quantities. When transferring x units from one bucket, the receiving bucket gains only x*(1-loss/100). Determine the greatest common water level achievable in all buckets. Return a real value within the source's specified tolerance; verify tolerance and loss bounds.

2152.task: Given points in a plane, return the fewest straight lines whose union contains every point. Lines may have any orientation and may cover several collinear points; a line can cover a single otherwise isolated point.

2158.task: Each day requests painting a half-open interval [start,end). Previously painted portions remain painted. Return the amount of previously unpainted length painted on each day, in chronological order.

2168.task: Given a digit string, count distinct substring texts in which every digit present has equal frequency. Different occurrences of the same substring text count only once; absent digits do not matter.

2174.task: Given a binary grid, one operation selects a cell currently containing 1 and changes every cell in its row and column to 0. Return the minimum operations to clear all ones. This is clearing, not toggling; verify this variant's operation before sharing code with 2128.

2184.task: Build a wall of given height and width using unlimited bricks of allowed widths in each row. Rows must exactly fill the width, and internal vertical seams cannot align between adjacent rows. Count distinct walls modulo 1000000007. Outer boundaries do not count as forbidden seams.

2204.task: Given a connected undirected graph with exactly one cycle, return each vertex's shortest distance in edges to any vertex on that cycle. Cycle vertices have distance zero. Verify the simple-graph and unique-cycle guarantees.

2214.task: A sequence of levels inflicts the given positive damage amounts. You may use armor once to reduce one level's damage by at most armor, never below zero. Find the minimum initial health that keeps health strictly positive after every level. All levels must be completed in order.

2219.task: For each array index, take the larger of the inclusive prefix sum ending there and inclusive suffix sum beginning there. Return the largest such score over all indices. Values may be negative; an empty prefix or suffix is not an option.

2229.task: Determine whether an integer array contains exactly one occurrence of each integer in some consecutive interval. Duplicates make the answer false, even when the maximum-minus-minimum span has the right size.

2237.task: Street positions are numbered 0 through n-1. Each light [position,range] contributes brightness one to positions within its inclusive range. Count positions whose total brightness meets or exceeds requirement[i]. Clip illumination to the street endpoints.

2247.task: Given an undirected weighted graph of cities and highways, find the greatest total highway cost of a simple trip using exactly k highways and therefore k+1 distinct cities. Return -1 if no such trip exists.

2254.task: Design a video platform with upload, remove, watch, like, dislike and getLikesAndDislikes/getViews operations. Upload assigns the smallest available nonnegative ID; removal frees it. watch returns the requested inclusive substring and increments views for an existing video. Return the prescribed missing-video sentinels for absent IDs. Verify exact method signatures and sentinels before certification.

2263.task: Given an integer array, change any element by +1 or -1 per operation. Return the fewest operations needed to make the array either nondecreasing or nonincreasing. Equal adjacent values are allowed; choose the cheaper orientation.

2268.task: Assign the lowercase alphabet to nine phone keys, each supporting up to three letters. A letter in the first, second or third slot costs that many presses. Given a string, choose the assignment minimizing total keypresses and return that minimum.

2277.task: Given an undirected tree and queries [start,end,node], return for each query the vertex on the unique start-to-end path closest in edge distance to node. The tree structure makes that nearest path vertex unique.

2282.task: People occupy a grid with given heights. For each person, count people visible looking right in the same row and down in the same column. A target is visible when every intervening height is strictly less than both endpoint heights. Verify distinct-height assumptions before handling equal blockers.

2291.task: Given current stock prices, future sale prices and a budget, buy at most one share of each stock so total purchase cost is at most budget. Return the maximum profit obtainable by selling the chosen shares at their future prices. Buying nothing is allowed.

2297.task: From index i, a jump to j>i is allowed when nums[i]<=nums[j] and every intermediate value is smaller than nums[i], or when nums[i]>nums[j] and every intermediate value is at least nums[i]. Jumping costs costs[j]. Find the minimum cost to reach the last index from the first; the starting cost is not paid. Verify these exact inequalities before certification.

2307.task: Equations specify positive ratios between named variables. Determine whether the equations contain a contradiction with any ratios implied by the others. Return a boolean, using the source's specified floating-point comparison tolerance. An equation connecting already-connected variables must agree with their implied ratio.

2313.task: A binary expression tree uses leaves 0/1 and operators OR, AND, XOR and NOT. Return the minimum number of leaf-bit flips needed to make the root evaluate to a requested boolean result. NOT has one child. Verify the numeric encoding of each operator before parsing nodes.

2323.task: Given equal-length arrays of job workloads and worker speeds, assign one worker to each job. A worker's time is the ceiling of workload divided by speed. Minimize the maximum completion time over all assignments and return it.

2330.task: Given a string, decide whether changing at most two characters to arbitrary letters can make it a palindrome. Changing a character costs one regardless of the replacement; insertion, deletion and rearrangement are not allowed.

2340.task: Using adjacent swaps, make an array valid by moving an occurrence of its minimum to the first position and an occurrence of its maximum to the last. Return the minimum number of swaps; other elements have no required final order.

2345.task: Mountains are isosceles right triangles with peaks (x,y), ground at y=0 and slopes ±1. Count peaks not covered by another mountain, including its boundary. Identical mountains hide each other rather than contributing multiple visible peaks. Verify this duplicate convention against the source.

2355.task: A row of shelves holds books[i] books. Choose a contiguous segment and take a positive number from each chosen shelf, never exceeding its supply, with taken counts strictly increasing from left to right. Return the maximum total books obtainable.

2361.task: Travel through successive stops on regular and express train lines. Starting on the regular line at stop zero, switching to express costs expressCost; switching back costs zero. Each segment has separate regular and express costs. Return the cheapest total cost to reach each subsequent stop, allowing either line on arrival.

2371.task: Replace a grid of distinct values with positive integers so every row and column preserves its original strict value ordering. Minimize the largest assigned integer and return any grid achieving that minimum. A whole-grid total order is not required.

2378.task: A rooted tree has a weight on each parent-child edge. Select edges with maximum total weight subject to no vertex touching more than one selected edge. Selecting no edges is allowed. Return the optimum weighted matching total.

2387.task: Given a matrix with an odd total number of elements and each row sorted, return its median value, counting all occurrences. Rows need not be ordered relative to one another.

2393.task: Count nonempty contiguous subarrays of an integer array whose values are strictly increasing from left to right. Every singleton qualifies.

2403.task: Monsters have required powers. Your energy starts at zero and grows by a current rate each day, initially one. Killing a monster requires accumulated energy at least its power, resets energy to zero and increases the growth rate by one. Choose the killing order to minimize total days. Verify exact day/action timing before certification.

2408.task: Implement an in-memory SQL-like store for named tables with fixed column counts. insertRow appends a row with a table-local increasing row ID starting at one; deleted IDs are not reused. deleteRow removes a row. selectCell returns a chosen column from a row. Verify one-based column indexing and valid-operation guarantees.

2417.task: An integer is fair when its decimal representation has equally many odd and even digits. Given positive n, return the smallest fair integer greater than or equal to n. Leading zeros are not part of a representation.

2422.task: Given a positive integer array, one operation replaces two adjacent elements with their sum. Return the minimum number of operations needed to make the resulting array a palindrome. Length one always qualifies.

2431.task: Fruits have prices and tastiness values; each fruit can be bought once. With a money budget and at most maxCoupons coupons, each halving one fruit's price using integer division, maximize total tastiness. At most one coupon applies to a fruit. Verify parameter names and exact rounding before certification.

2436.task: Partition an integer array into the fewest contiguous nonempty subarrays such that the gcd of every element in each subarray is greater than one. Return the minimum count. Verify the input guarantee ensuring a valid split, or the required failure output if one-valued elements occur.

2445.task: A complete binary tree with nodes numbered 1 through n initially has value zero everywhere. Each query toggles the value of every node in the queried node's subtree. Return how many nodes have value one after all queries. Children of i are 2i and 2i+1 when within n.

2450.task: Given a binary string and a fixed window length k, an operation flips all bits in any length-k contiguous window. Return the number of distinct binary strings reachable after any number of operations, modulo 1000000007. Verify that zero operations is included and k does not exceed length.

2459.task: An array is a permutation of 0 through n-1, where zero denotes an empty slot. One move swaps zero with another item. Return the minimum moves to reach either sorted occupied-item order with zero first ([0,1,...]) or zero last ([1,2,...,0]). Verify the two accepted target configurations.

2464.task: Split an integer array into contiguous nonempty pieces so the gcd of the first and last value of every piece is greater than one. Return the minimum number of pieces, or -1 if impossible. Interior values do not participate in that piece's endpoint condition.

2473.task: An undirected road graph has travel costs, and each city sells an apple at a given price. For each starting city, choose where to buy one apple and return home. Outbound road cost is normal; return road cost is multiplied by k. Return the minimum total cost for every starting city, including buying locally with no travel. Verify the return-cost multiplier convention.

2479.task: Given a rooted tree with positive node values, choose two disjoint rooted subtrees and maximize the bitwise XOR of their subtree sums. Return zero if no such pair exists. Disjoint means neither selected root is an ancestor of the other.

2489.task: Given a binary string and positive ratio parameters, count contiguous substrings whose numbers of zeros and ones have the requested fixed ratio. The exact parameter ordering must be verified before implementing the adapter; do not infer which parameter belongs to which bit.

2495.task: Given an integer array, count nonempty contiguous subarrays whose product is even. Products need not be materialized: a product is even exactly when the subarray contains an even value.

2505.task: Given a nonnegative integer array, consider the sum of every subsequence, including all choices of indices. Return the bitwise OR of these sums. Duplicated values remain independently selectable. Verify the result's required integer width.

2510.task: Given a binary matrix, determine whether a path from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down contains equally many zeros and ones, counting both endpoints.

2519.task: An index is k-big when at least k elements strictly smaller than nums[i] occur before it and at least k strictly smaller elements occur after it. Count such indices; occurrences count separately.

2533.task: Count binary strings with lengths in [minLength,maxLength] that can be constructed by appending blocks of zeroGroup zeros or oneGroup ones in any order. Return the count modulo 1000000007. Verify the exact named-parameter order in the source.

2534.task: People arrive at integer times to use one door, taking one second each, with direction 0 for entering and 1 for exiting. When both directions wait, reuse the previous second's direction if the door was used; if it was idle, exiting has priority. Within a direction, earlier input index wins. Return each person's crossing time.

2539.task: Count nonempty subsequences of a lowercase string such that every character appearing in the subsequence appears the same number of times. Count different index selections separately and return the result modulo 1000000007.

2548.task: Items have prices and weights. Fill a bag of capacity at most capacity, allowing fractional quantities of an item, to maximize total price. Return -1 if the available total weight cannot fill the requested capacity. Verify whether the task requires the bag exactly full, the item-field order and numeric tolerance before certification.

2557.task: Choose distinct integers from 1 through n excluding banned values, with total sum at most maxSum. Return the maximum number selectable. Banned duplicates do not ban extra numbers; bounds require an approach that need not enumerate the whole range.

2590.task: Design a task manager with addTask, getAllTasks, getTasksForTag and completeTask. Tasks have globally assigned increasing IDs, user ownership, descriptions, due dates and tags. Queries return only uncompleted tasks for that user ordered by due date, optionally restricted by tag. Completion by a different user must not complete the task. Verify tie guarantees and exact method signatures.

2599.task: Reorder an integer array by repeatedly taking one element and moving it to the end. Return the fewest such operations needed so every prefix sum is nonnegative. Relative order of unmoved elements is preserved. Verify the guarantee that the total sum is nonnegative.

2604.task: Hens and grains occupy positions on a line. Hens move simultaneously at unit speed and can consume grains they reach. Return the minimum elapsed time until every grain has been eaten, assigning any number of grains to each hen. A hen may change direction; grains do not move.

2618.task: Implement checkIfInstanceOfClass(obj,classFunction), returning whether the object belongs to the supplied class or an ancestor class through the prototype chain. Handle null/undefined and invalid class arguments without throwing. The remembered contract also recognizes primitive values through their wrapper classes; verify that behavior before using plain instanceof alone.

2619.task: Add Array.prototype.last, returning the array's final element or -1 when empty. Do not mutate the array.

2620.task: Implement createCounter(n), returning a function that yields n on its first call and increments the returned integer by one on each subsequent call. Each counter has independent state.

2621.task: Implement async sleep(millis), returning a promise that resolves after approximately the requested delay. The resolved value is unspecified; avoid blocking the event loop.

2622.task: Implement TimeLimitedCache with set(key,value,duration), get(key) and count(). Keys expire duration milliseconds after their latest set. set returns whether an unexpired value already existed and replaces its value/expiry. get returns -1 for absent or expired keys; count includes only unexpired entries. Old timers must not delete newer replacements.

2623.task: Implement memoize(fn), returning a function caching fn's result by its argument list. Repeated calls with the same arguments must not recompute fn; argument order matters. The simpler task uses the supplied numeric-function cases; verify supported domains rather than claiming arbitrary-object equality.

2624.task: Add snail(rowsCount,colsCount) to Array. If the dimensions do not multiply to the input length, return []. Otherwise fill a rowsCount-by-colsCount matrix column by column, alternating top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top. Preserve every input occurrence exactly once.

2625.task: Given a nested array and depth n, return a new array flattened by at most n nested levels. With n=0 preserve the top-level nesting. Do not use the built-in flat method; preserve value order.

2626.task: Implement reduce(nums,fn,init), applying fn(accumulator,currentValue) from left to right starting at init and returning the final accumulator. An empty array returns init. Do not call the built-in Array.reduce.

2627.task: Implement debounce(fn,t), returning a function that schedules fn for t milliseconds after the latest call and cancels any prior pending invocation. Invoke with the most recent call's arguments; a quiet interval permits one invocation. Verify any required this-binding contract.

2628.task: Implement areDeeplyEqual(o1,o2) for JSON-compatible values. Compare primitive values, array length/order and corresponding elements, and object key sets/values recursively. Object key order does not matter. Arrays and ordinary objects are different kinds; null is not an object to traverse.

2629.task: Given an array of unary functions, return their right-to-left composition: the last function receives the input first. An empty function list produces the identity function.

2630.task: Implement memoize(fn) for arbitrary argument values using argument identity rather than JSON serialization. A cached result is reused only when each argument matches the corresponding previous argument by the specified strict-identity semantics. Argument order and argument count matter; verify the source's NaN and this-binding expectations.

2631.task: Add Array.prototype.groupBy(fn). Apply fn to each element to obtain its group key and return an object mapping keys to arrays of original elements in their original relative order. Do not use a built-in groupBy implementation.

2632.task: Implement curry(fn), allowing a function's required arguments to be supplied over successive calls, with each call able to supply multiple arguments. Invoke fn once enough arguments have accumulated and return its result. Before then, return a function accepting more arguments. Verify over-application and zero-argument-function behavior.

2633.task: Serialize a JSON-compatible value into a valid JSON string without JSON.stringify. Support null, booleans, finite numbers, strings, arrays and objects. Preserve array order and emit correct punctuation/string quoting. Verify the source's string-escape restrictions; do not assume arbitrary strings contain no escapes unless stated.

2634.task: Implement filter(arr,fn), returning elements for which fn(value,index) is truthy, in their original order. Do not use Array.filter and do not mutate the input.

2635.task: Implement map(arr,fn), returning fn(value,index) for each input element in order. Do not use Array.map and do not mutate the input.

2636.task: Given functions that return promises and a concurrency limit n, execute all while at most n function calls are still unresolved. Start another as soon as a slot frees. Return a promise resolving when every task finishes. Verify the source's rejection guarantees before choosing an error policy.

2637.task: Implement timeLimit(fn,t), returning an async wrapper. Forward its arguments to fn. Resolve or reject with fn's outcome if it settles in time; otherwise reject with 'Time Limit Exceeded' after t milliseconds. Clear obsolete timers and avoid unhandled late rejections.

2638.task: Given distinct integers and positive k, count subsets that do not contain two numbers whose absolute difference is k. Include the empty subset. Verify the source's modulo or integer-range requirements before fixing the output type.

2648.task: Implement a generator producing the infinite Fibonacci sequence 0,1,1,2,3,5,..., yielding one number per next() request and maintaining state between yields.

2649.task: Implement a generator that traverses a nested array of integers depth-first from left to right and yields each integer. Empty arrays yield nothing; do not yield array containers.

2650.task: Implement a cancellable runner for a generator that yields promises. Resume it with resolved values and throw rejection reasons back into the generator. Return a cancellation function and a completion promise. Cancellation throws 'Cancelled' into the generator so it can handle the event; complete with its return value or uncaught error. Verify cancellation race rules against the source.

2655.task: Given an inclusive integer range [0,n-1] and covered inclusive subranges, return the maximal uncovered ranges in increasing order. Merge overlapping or adjacent covered ranges before identifying gaps. Verify the input endpoint convention.

2664.task: Given board dimensions and a start square, construct a knight's tour visiting every square exactly once and label squares by visit order starting at zero. Return a valid labeling; verify whether the input guarantees a tour and what failure result is required otherwise.

2665.task: Implement createCounter(init) returning increment, decrement and reset methods sharing one value. Increment/decrement change it by one and return the new value; reset restores init and returns it.

2666.task: Implement once(fn), returning a wrapper that invokes fn only on its first call and returns that result. Later calls return undefined without invoking fn again. Preserve the first call's arguments.

2667.task: Implement createHelloWorld(), returning a function that returns the exact string 'Hello World' regardless of supplied arguments.

2674.task: Given a nonempty circular singly linked list, split it into two circular lists preserving original order. The first receives ceil(n/2) nodes starting at the original head and the second receives the remainder. Verify minimum-length guarantees and the required representation of an empty second half.

2675.task: Given an array of JSON objects, create a matrix whose first row contains the lexicographically sorted union of all flattened leaf paths using dot separators. Subsequent rows contain each object's leaf value for each path, or an empty string when absent. Arrays contribute numeric path components; null is a leaf. Verify empty-container treatment and dot-containing-key guarantees.

2676.task: Implement throttle(fn,t). The first call invokes immediately. During the next t milliseconds, suppress calls but remember the latest arguments; at the boundary invoke once with those arguments if any arrived, then start another t-window. Continue until no pending call remains. Verify exact boundary scheduling and this-binding expectations.

2677.task: Split an array into consecutive chunks of positive size, with a possibly shorter final chunk. Preserve order and return an empty list for empty input. Do not invent padding values.

2689.task: A rope tree stores literal strings at leaves and concatenations at internal nodes, with length metadata. Return the kth character of the represented string using the metadata to avoid full expansion. Verify whether k is one-based and exactly which subtree length each node stores before implementing navigation.

2690.task: Implement createInfiniteObject(), returning an object for which calling any string-named property as a method returns that property's name. A Proxy can implement dynamic methods without predeclaring their names. Verify symbol-property behavior only if included in the source domain.

2691.task: Implement the specified immutable-update helper so applying changes produces a new value while leaving the original unchanged and sharing unchanged substructures where required. The exact helper API and supported mutation syntax are not reliably known from memory; this is an incomplete draft and must not be implemented from the title alone.

2692.task: Create a wrapper that prevents mutations to an object and nested objects/arrays while allowing reads. Block assignment, deletion and mutating collection methods according to the source's contract. The exact required exception strings and supported operations need source verification; this draft is incomplete.

2693.task: Implement a custom callPolyfill method for functions, invoking the function with the supplied context as this and forwarding remaining arguments. Preserve its return value without using the forbidden built-in call/apply/bind operations. Verify primitive/null-context semantics and allowed language features.

2694.task: Implement EventEmitter.subscribe(eventName,callback), returning an object with unsubscribe, and emit(eventName,args), returning callback results in subscription order. Multiple subscriptions coexist; unsubscribing removes only that subscription. No subscribers yields an empty result array.

2695.task: Implement ArrayWrapper around a numeric array. Numeric coercion, such as adding two wrappers, yields the sum of stored elements. String coercion yields bracketed comma-separated values, such as '[4,7]'. An empty wrapper converts numerically to zero and textually to '[]'.

2700.task: Given two JSON-compatible objects, return their differing values at shared keys as [oldValue,newValue], recursively retaining nested shared-key differences. Keys present on only one side are ignored. Arrays compare shared numeric indices. Verify how differing container types are represented in the expected result.

2702.task: Given positive integers and x>y, an operation chooses one element to reduce by x while reducing every other element by y. Return the minimum operations needed to make all values nonpositive. Elements may go below zero.

2703.task: Implement argumentsLength(...args), returning how many arguments were passed, including explicit undefined values.

2704.task: Implement expect(val) with toBe(other) and notToBe(other), using strict equality. Successful assertions return true. Failed toBe throws Error('Not Equal'); failed notToBe throws Error('Equal').

2705.task: Recursively compact a JSON object or array by removing properties/elements with falsy values. Preserve truthy nested containers while compacting their contents, preserve array order and do not treat an empty object or array as falsy.

2714.task: Given a weighted graph, source, destination and k, find the minimum travel cost when up to k traversed edges may be taken at zero cost. Each free hop is optional. Verify graph directionality and unreachable-output conventions before certification.

2715.task: Implement cancellable(fn,args,t), scheduling fn(...args) after t milliseconds and returning a function that cancels the pending invocation when called before it runs. Cancellation after execution must not run fn again.

2721.task: Implement promiseAll(functions), invoking every zero-argument promise-returning function and returning a promise for their resolved values in input order. Reject upon a task rejection; resolve to [] for no functions. Do not use Promise.all.

2722.task: Join two arrays of objects by id. Keep every distinct id; when both arrays contain it, merge properties with the second array overriding collisions. Return objects sorted by numeric id. Verify the guarantee that each individual input has unique ids.

2723.task: Given two promises resolving to numbers, return a promise resolving to the sum of their values after both resolve.

2724.task: Sort an array by the numeric values returned from a provided fn, in ascending order. Return the sorted array. Verify whether fn is guaranteed to produce unique keys before assuming ties cannot occur.

2725.task: Implement cancellable(fn,args,t), invoking fn(...args) immediately and every t milliseconds afterward. Return a function stopping future interval invocations when called. This differs from the one-shot timeout-cancellation problem.

2726.task: Implement a Calculator supporting chainable add, subtract, multiply, divide and power operations on its stored value, plus getResult. Each arithmetic method returns the calculator itself. Dividing by zero throws Error('Division by zero is not allowed').

2727.task: Return whether a JSON object or array contains no own enumerable keys/elements. Empty arrays and empty objects return true; objects with a key whose value is null are not empty.

2728.task: A street is a circular doubly linked collection of houses exposed through door-open/close and left/right movement methods. Count the houses using only that interface. Verify the allowed methods, initial door states and the provided upper-bound parameter; this draft does not supply those hidden-interface details.

2737.task: Given a directed weighted graph, a starting vertex and a set of marked vertices, return the minimum path cost from the start to any marked vertex, or -1 if none is reachable. Starting at a marked vertex has cost zero.

2743.task: Given a string, count nonempty contiguous substrings with no repeated character. Count positional occurrences even if their text is equal.

2754.task: Implement a function-binding utility that returns a function invoking the original with a fixed this context and any prebound arguments followed by call-time arguments. Verify the exact required prototype method name, constructor behavior and built-in restrictions before certification.

2755.task: Deep-merge two JSON-compatible values. Recursively merge matching object keys and array indices; when types do not both support recursive merging, the second value replaces the first. Retain first-only keys/indices and include second-only ones. Verify null handling and whether mutation of inputs is permitted.

2756.task: Implement request batching so calls made within the specified time window are collected into one underlying batch query and each caller receives the corresponding result. The exact batch timing, API signature and error routing are not reliably known from memory; obtain the source before implementation.

2757.task: Implement a generator over a circular array starting at a specified index. Yield the current element; each next(jump) moves by that signed jump before the next yield, wrapping modulo array length. Verify the default jump and initial next-argument behavior required by the source.

2758.task: Add a nextDay method to a Date object that returns the following calendar date formatted YYYY-MM-DD. Verify the required timezone/local-versus-UTC semantics before using millisecond arithmetic across daylight-saving transitions.

2759.task: Parse a JSON string into its corresponding JavaScript value without JSON.parse or eval. Support the source's stated JSON grammar, including nested arrays/objects and primitive values. Verify any restricted grammar guarantees; do not silently ignore escapes or number syntax.

2764.task: Given a sequence of [node,parent] pairs describing a binary tree traversal, determine whether it can be a preorder traversal of the described tree. Each subtree must occupy one contiguous segment and every parent precede its children. Verify sentinel, distinctness and child-order assumptions before certification.

2773.task: A special binary tree has extra leaf links connecting leaves in a doubly linked chain instead of ordinary null child pointers. Return the genuine tree height without following those leaf links as descendants. Verify the exact head/tail linkage convention and whether height counts edges or nodes.

2774.task: Implement an upper-bound search over a sorted numeric array to return the last index whose value equals target, or -1 if absent. Verify the requested method name and whether the problem instead defines an insertion index; the remembered version returns the final occurrence.

2775.task: Recursively replace undefined values with null in a nested object/array while preserving other values and structure. Verify the source's mutation requirement and whether sparse array holes count as values to replace.

2776.task: Convert a callback-style asynchronous function into a promise-returning one. Forward arguments and translate callback success/error into resolution/rejection. Verify the exact callback argument convention before implementing: an error-first callback cannot be assumed from the title alone.

2777.task: Implement a generator yielding formatted dates from a given start through a given end at the specified day step. Verify whether endpoints are inclusive, the exact format, timezone semantics and allowed step signs before certification.

2782.task: An opaque CategoryHandler.haveSameCategory(a,b) reports whether two indexed elements belong to the same hidden category. Given the number of elements, return the number of distinct categories using only this equivalence query. Verify the query-call limit if one is specified.

2794.task: Given parallel keys and values arrays, return an object formed by pairing them. When a key occurs more than once, keep its first paired value in the remembered specification. Verify the duplicate rule and key string-coercion behavior before certification.

2795.task: Execute all supplied promise-returning functions concurrently and return an outcome record for each in input order, preserving both successes and failures instead of rejecting the entire operation. Verify the exact expected result-record schema before implementation.

2796.task: Implement a string repeat method returning n consecutive copies of the original string without using the built-in repeat. For n=0 return an empty string. Verify nonnegative-integer input guarantees.

2797.task: Implement partial(fn,args), where '_' placeholders in the stored argument list are filled left to right from later call arguments; remaining call arguments are appended. Return fn's result from the assembled argument list. Verify behavior when fewer arguments than placeholders are supplied.

2802.task: A lucky number uses only decimal digits 4 and 7. Given positive k, return the kth lucky number in increasing numeric order, starting 4,7,44,47,74,77,... . Use an integer representation large enough for the official bounds.

2803.task: Implement a generator yielding factorial values in sequence while maintaining its running product. Verify whether the source starts at 0! or 1!; both equal one but determine whether the first two yields repeat one.

2804.task: Implement Array.prototype.forEach with a callback and optional thisArg, invoking the callback in array order with value, index and the array. Return undefined. Verify the required treatment of holes and concurrent length changes; full native semantics should not be assumed absent a specification.

2805.task: Implement a custom recurring timer whose successive delays follow the supplied delay/period formula and expose cancellation. The exact timing recurrence and API are not reliably known from memory, so this is an incomplete draft pending the source.

2814.task: In a grid, water spreads to neighboring traversable cells each minute while a traveler moves one step per minute from start to destination. Return the shortest safe travel time or -1. Verify terrain symbols, whether destination floods, and whether flooding happens before movement; these details materially change reachability.

2821.task: Given promises and a delay, return corresponding promises whose outcomes are delayed as specified. Verify whether delay begins at invocation or each original settlement, and whether rejections are delayed; the title alone does not settle these timing rules.

2822.task: Invert a JSON object by using each original value's string representation as a key and its original key as the value. If several original keys map to the same inverted key, retain all such keys in an array. Verify array ordering and the supported primitive-value domain.

2823.task: Recursively filter a nested JSON object/array by a predicate, retaining qualifying leaves and their necessary container structure and removing empty results. Verify whether the predicate applies to containers, the empty-root sentinel and whether arrays preserve holes; this draft is incomplete without that contract.

2832.task: For each element of an integer array, return the length of the largest contiguous range containing its index in which it is a maximum. Verify whether equal values are allowed in that range or the element must be the unique/strict maximum before selecting stack comparisons.

2838.task: Heroes and monsters have strengths, and each monster has a coin reward. For each hero, return the total coins from monsters the hero can defeat independently of other heroes. Verify whether defeat uses strength >= or >; do not infer it from the title.

2847.task: Given a positive integer n, return the smallest positive integer whose decimal digits multiply to n, or the source's failure sentinel when impossible. Verify whether the result is returned as a string and whether n=1 returns '1' before implementing the adapter.

2852.task: A grid contains nonnegative values and blocked cells. For each unblocked cell, its remoteness is the sum of values of unblocked cells it cannot reach by four-direction moves avoiding blocked cells. Return the sum of remoteness across all unblocked cells. Verify the blocked sentinel and numeric bounds.

2863.task: Find the maximum length of a contiguous subarray of length at least two whose first element is strictly greater than its last element. Return zero if none exists. Interior values impose no ordering condition.

2877.task: Pandas: given student_data as rows of [student_id,age], create and return a DataFrame with columns student_id and age in that order. Preserve row order.

2878.task: Pandas: given a DataFrame, return a two-element list containing its row count and column count, in that order.

2879.task: Pandas: return the first three rows of the supplied employees DataFrame, preserving all columns and original row order. If fewer than three rows exist, return all rows.

2880.task: Pandas: from a students DataFrame with student_id, name and age, select the record with student_id equal to 101 and return only name and age columns. Verify the target ID against the source before certification.

2881.task: Pandas: add a bonus column to an employees DataFrame, with each bonus equal to twice that employee's salary. Return the DataFrame with the new column and existing columns retained.

2882.task: Pandas: remove duplicate rows based on the email column, retaining the first occurrence for each email and preserving retained-row order. Other columns are not part of the duplicate key.

2883.task: Pandas: remove student rows with missing name values and return the remaining DataFrame. Do not remove a row merely because another column is missing.

2884.task: Pandas: double every value in the employees DataFrame's salary column and return the updated table with its other columns retained.

2885.task: Pandas: rename students columns id→student_id, first→first_name, last→last_name and age→age_in_years, returning the DataFrame without changing data values. Verify those exact source column names before certification.

2886.task: Pandas: convert the grade column of the students DataFrame to integer dtype and return the table. Verify missing-value and conversion guarantees; do not invent rounding rules for nonintegral grades.

2887.task: Pandas: fill missing values in the products DataFrame's quantity column with zero, leaving existing quantities and other columns unchanged.

2888.task: Pandas: vertically concatenate df1 and df2 into one DataFrame, retaining all rows in input-table order. Verify whether the expected index must be reset or is ignored by the evaluator.

2889.task: Pandas: pivot weather data so rows correspond to month, columns to city and cells contain temperature. Verify the source's duplicate city/month guarantee before choosing pivot rather than an aggregation.

2890.task: Pandas: reshape sales data from one row per product with separate quarter columns into long form with product, quarter and sales. Preserve the quarter labels as values; verify exact input column names and output order requirements.

2891.task: Pandas: using chained operations, select animals heavier than 100 from a table of animal names and weights, sort by weight descending, and return only the name column. Verify the exact table/column names and strict threshold against the source.

2892.task: Repeatedly replace two adjacent elements by their product only when that product is at most k. Return the minimum possible final array length. Verify the positive-integer domain, because zeros or negatives would change the greedy grouping argument.

2898.task: Given stock prices indexed by day, choose a subsequence whose price differences equal the corresponding day-index differences, so all selected price-minus-index values agree. Maximize the sum of chosen prices and return it. Verify one-based versus zero-based notation and whether all prices are positive.
